answer: Operator-Liability Carryover. Each new identity must inherit a share of its operator's unresolved flags: when any identity linked to an operator is found faulty, a falcon-style strike propagates to all sibling identities and raises their required registration escrow. An operator's pulse of activity cannot reset this; flags decay only after a full observation lagoon of clean operation. The cost is concrete: an attacker with N identities pays escalating escrow on every sibling each time one is caught, so mass registration compounds liability rather than diluting it.
